name: Sugar, sucrose
description: Plain white sugar. FSSAI lets a pack write just 'Sugar' for sucrose {1}. Cane sugar is the same sugar. Sugar syrup is sugar melted in water.

name: Brown sugar, raw cane sugar
description: Sugar with some molasses left in or added back.

name: Cane juice, sugarcane juice
description: Juice pressed from sugarcane, dried or boiled down.

name: Khandsari, khaand, bura, misri
description: Traditional Indian sugars. FSSAI has a standard for khandsari, bura and misri {3}.

name: Jaggery, gur, gud, shakkar
description: Cane or palm juice boiled down into a block or powder {3}. FSSAI has a standard for it {3}. ICMR-NIN lists jaggery as an added sugar {5}.

name: Coconut sugar, palm sugar
description: Sugar made from palm sap.

name: Dextrose, glucose
description: A simple sugar. FSSAI lets a pack write 'Dextrose' or 'Glucose' for it {1}.

name: Trehalose
description: A sugar made of two glucose units. It counts as a sugar under FSSAI's definition {1}.

name: Liquid glucose, glucose syrup
description: A sweet syrup. FSSAI's rules for sweets list liquid glucose as a sweetener {4}.

name: Dried glucose syrup, glucose syrup solids
description: Glucose syrup dried into a powder. FSSAI has a standard for it {3}.

name: Invert sugar, invert syrup, golden syrup
description: Sugar split into glucose and fructose. FSSAI defines golden syrup as sugar syrup that has been split this way {3}.

name: Fructose, fruit sugar
description: A simple sugar. ICMR-NIN names fructose as a hidden sugar {5}.

name: Corn syrup, high-fructose corn syrup
description: Syrups made from corn starch. ICMR-NIN names corn syrup as a hidden sugar {5}.

name: Rice syrup, maple syrup, agave
description: Sweet syrups. WHO counts the sugars in syrups as free sugars (sugar added to food, plus honey, syrups and juice) {7}.

name: Maltose, malt extract, malt syrup
description: Maltose counts as a sugar under FSSAI's definition {1}. Malt extract is a sweet syrup or powder made from malted grain.

name: Lactose
description: Milk sugar. It counts as a sugar under FSSAI's definition {1}, and FSSAI's rules for sweets list it as a sweetener {4}.

name: Honey
description: WHO counts the sugar in honey as free sugar {7}.

name: Molasses
description: The dark syrup left over when sugar is made. ICMR-NIN names it as a hidden sugar {5}.

name: Fruit juice concentrate
description: Juice with the water taken out. WHO counts it as free sugar {7}. A 'no added sugar' food cannot use it in place of sugar {2}. Plain fruit juice also counts as free sugar for WHO {7}. Lemon and lime juice concentrate are used for sourness, so the checker does not count them.

name: Date paste, date syrup, dried fruit paste
description: Fruit cooked down into a paste or syrup. A 'no added sugar' food cannot use dried fruit paste in place of sugar {2}.

name: Jam, jelly, sweetened chocolate, sweetened fruit pieces
description: Sugary ingredients. A 'no added sugar' food cannot contain them {2}.

name: Sweetened condensed milk
description: Milk boiled down with a lot of sugar added. Unsweetened condensed milk is not counted.

name: Maltodextrin
description: Maltodextrin is made from starch, as chains of glucose. Most of it is not a sugar in FSSAI's legal definition {1}, so most of it shows in the carbohydrate line, not the sugar line.

name: Maltitol, sorbitol
description: Sweeteners made from sugar, with fewer calories. They are not sugars in law, so the tool does not count them. ICMR-NIN says to watch for maltitol in sugar free foods {5}.
